visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: A stock trades at €20. Your target is €26 and your downside case is €16. What's the risk-reward?

options.text: 2 to 1

questions.explain: Six euros up against four down: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 to 1. The 30% upside on its own is only half a pitch.
questions.explain_at: That's a risk-reward of one and a half to one

questions.q: You pitch a stock because it's a wonderful company. What's missing?

options.text: A higher price target for the shares
Why the market has it wrong
More on the brand and the margins
A longer time to hold the stock

questions.explain: A wonderful company is usually priced as one. A pitch says what's priced in and where your view differs.
questions.explain_at: A good company and a good stock aren't the same thing

questions.q: What is a catalyst in a markets pitch?

options.text: A strong brand that keeps customers
The price at which you'd sell out
A fall that makes the shares cheap
An event that makes the market see it

questions.explain: An event, ideally with a date, such as a contract award or a vote. Without one, you're waiting for the market to notice eventually.

questions.q: Mobico's shares are at 40p against a 46p offer, and would fall to 30p if the deal broke. Roughly what chance of completion does that price imply?

options.text: About 62%
About 13%
About 87%
About 38%

questions.explain: What you can lose over the whole range: 10 ÷ (6 + 10) ≈ 62%. Six over forty-six is the gain as a share of the offer, not a probability.

questions.q: Mobico's equity is worth about £308m at the offer price, and its enterprise value about £2.3bn. What does that mean for shareholders?

options.text: They receive the full £2.3bn
Debt comes first, so the shares swing more
The buyer is overpaying by about £2bn
Their equity is the safest claim

questions.explain: Debt and other claims rank ahead, so the equity is less than a seventh of the business, and small changes in its value move the shares a lot.
questions.explain_at: the equity is less than a seventh of the business
